hints: Start by recalling what PVC is made from and what type of polymerisation forms it.
Write out the monomer chloroethene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$, and see what happens to its double bond when it joins the chain.
Compare the atom ratio in one monomer with the atom ratio in one repeat unit to decide about the empirical formula.
walkthrough:
**Identify the monomer and polymer type**

PVC is poly(chloroethene), an addition polymer. Its monomer is chloroethene, also called vinyl chloride.

$$n\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl} \rightarrow \text{-[CH}_2\text{-CHCl]-}_n$$

**Check saturation and the repeat unit**

In addition polymerisation the C=C double bond opens to form two new C-C single bonds. So the polymer chain is saturated, with repeat unit $\text{-[CH}_2\text{-CHCl]-}$.

That repeat unit contains 2 C, 3 H and 1 Cl.

**Compare empirical formulas**

The monomer $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$ has molecular formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl}$, which is already its simplest ratio. The polymer is $(\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl})_n$, so its simplest ratio is also $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl}$.

Addition polymerisation just joins monomers together with no small molecule lost, so the empirical formula stays the same.

**Check combustion products**

Burning a chlorinated polymer releases hydrogen chloride, $\text{HCl}$, which dissolves to give a strongly acidic gas, not alkaline. It is harmful to breathe in because it is acidic and toxic.

options.A: Incorrect. Combustion of PVC produces $\text{HCl}$ gas plus $\text{CO}$ and $\text{CO}_2$. $\text{HCl}$ is strongly acidic, not alkaline, though it is indeed harmful to breathe in.
options.B: Correct. Monomer $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$ is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl}$ and repeat unit $\text{-[CH}_2\text{-CHCl]-}$ is also $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{Cl}$. Since addition polymerisation loses no atoms, the empirical formula is unchanged.
options.C: Incorrect. The monomer is unsaturated due to C=C, but polymerisation breaks the pi bond to link monomers. PVC has only C-C single bonds in its backbone, so it is saturated.
options.D: Incorrect. The repeat unit of PVC is $\text{-[CH}_2\text{-CHCl]-}$, from chloroethene. $\text{-[CH}_2\text{-CCl}_2\text{]-}$ is the repeat unit of poly(vinylidene chloride), from $\text{CH}_2=\text{CCl}_2$.
